candidates.exact_span: Unless otherwise indicated in this permit, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or pollutant parameter is sufficiently sensitive (as defined above) and the analytical test result is less than the MQL, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs. Furthermore, if the EPA Region 6 MQL for a pollutant or parameter is not sufficiently sensitive, but the analytical test result is less than the published ML from a sufficiently sensitive method, then a value of zero (0) may be used for reporting purposes on DMRs.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of when sub-MQL or sub-ML results may be reported as zero affects which numeric value is compared against enforceable limits (Purpose A) and how no-result or below-detection reporting is classified versus ordinary numeric results (Purpose C).

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, B. AUTHORIZED DISCHARGES
candidates.exact_span: Discharges authorized in this individual permit are limited to once through cooling water, cooling tower blowdown, and storm water from the adjacent areas.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Which discharge types are authorized determines whether monitoring obligations attach to a given outfall or activity and whether a period without discharge from unauthorized sources should be treated as a documented no-discharge or conditional non-applicability state.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, B. AUTHORIZED DISCHARGES
candidates.exact_span: There shall be no discharge of domestic sewage into waters of the United States.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A categorical prohibition on domestic sewage discharge affects whether monitoring and limit comparisons are applicable to domestic sewage flows and how absence of such discharges is characterized in missing-evidence analysis.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, B. AUTHORIZED DISCHARGES
candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from outfalls other than Outfalls 001 shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Routing non-001 storm water to a different permit affects which enforceable numeric limits apply at those outfalls (Purpose A) and which permit's monitoring requirements govern them (Purpose B).

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, B. AUTHORIZED DISCHARGES
candidates.exact_span: Runoffs from active quarry areas are not authorized.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether quarry runoff is unauthorized versus conditionally allowed elsewhere in the segment changes whether monitoring is required for quarry-area flows and how no-discharge or unauthorized-discharge periods are established.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE, item 2
candidates.exact_span: Discharges are restricted to overflows from the retention pond due to catastrophic or chronic precipitation events.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The event-conditioned authorization of discharge affects when monitoring obligations are triggered by discharge occurrence and whether periods without qualifying overflow events are documented conditional non-requirement or unresolved no-data states.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE, item 3
candidates.exact_span: Discharges of storm water runoff from access roads in undisturbed areas shall be covered under the NPDES Multi-Sector Storm Water Permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Assigning access-road storm water to the Multi-Sector permit rather than this permit changes which monitoring requirements are actually applicable for those flows.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, C. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICE, item 4
candidates.exact_span: If a discharge of storm runoff from a quarry (mining) area is necessary, the discharge must comply with effluent limitations established at Outfall 001.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Linking necessary quarry-area storm runoff to Outfall 001 effluent limitations determines which numeric limits apply for comparison (Purpose A) and whether monitoring tied to Outfall 001 becomes applicable when such a discharge occurs (Purpose B).

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, D. REOPENER CLAUSE
candidates.exact_span: If the State re-evaluates and updates the total maximum daily loads (TMDL) or final effluent limitation necessary to protect water quality standards during the life of this permit, and the effluent limitations are more stringent than those listed in this permit, or controls a pollutant not listed in this permit, then the permit may be modified or revoked and reissued to conform with the approved Water Quality Management Plan (WQMP) final effluent limitations.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether and when TMDL-driven modifications took effect during Federal FY2025 could change which enforceable numeric discharge limits are in force for evaluated measurements.

candidates.locator: page 7, section part_i, E. WHOLE EFFLUENT TOXICITY TESTING (7 DAY CHRONIC NOEC)
candidates.exact_span: It is unlawful and a violation of this permit for a permittee or his designated agent, to manipulate test samples in any manner, to delay sample shipment, or to terminate or to cause to terminate a toxicity test. Once initiated, all toxicity tests must be completed unless specific authority has been granted by EPA Region 6 or the State NPDES permitting authority.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Mandatory completion of initiated WET tests and restrictions on termination affect whether WET monitoring was required to produce a valid result (Purpose B) and whether an absent or incomplete result reflects documented conditional non-requirement, inadequate evidence, or an unresolved missing-evidence case (Purpose C).
